Thanks for the ping — quick read and proposed approach below. I ran a VIES check while drafting (DE123456789 returned VALID). Notes:

1) High-level: This appears to be B2B cross-border EU supply of services. With a valid VAT ID for a business customer in another member state, the correct treatment is typically reverse-charge (we issue a net invoice; recipient self-accounts for VAT in their jurisdiction). We should NOT charge German VAT.

2) OSS nuance: OSS only applies when the supplier collects VAT on sales of services to consumers (B2C) or certain cross-border supplies of goods/telecoms — it does not override reverse-charge for B2B with a valid VAT ID. Atlas's OSS registration in DE is not a reason for Redwood to collect VAT on a B2B sale.

3) Practical invoice edit (recommended):
- Line: Platform service — EUR 10,000.00 (net)
- Line: Marketplace fee — EUR 2,000.00 (net)
- VAT: Reverse-charge — VAT 0.00 (Customer to account per Article 196)
- Total due: EUR 12,000.00 (net)
- Add note: "VAT reverse charge — Article 196. VAT ID validated via VIES: DE123456789."

4) Accounting treatment and AR: Mark invoice as "B2B reverse-charge — EU" and attach VIES validation screenshot + atlas_vat_cert.jpg. No VAT posting on our GL for this transaction.

5) Payment release: we can release net amount once attachments are archived. If legal needs to sign-off for large sums (>EUR 50k) we escalate, but this one is within normal limits.

If you want I can draft the exact wording to add to the invoice and a short email we send back to Atlas to confirm.
